How many text units (paragraph or sentence, depending on the voice engine) guided reading prepares ahead of the one currently playing. Applies to every voice engine. Further ahead: less chance of silence between chunks, but uses more memory/battery and may synthesize text you never end up hearing if you jump to a different spot. Less ahead: saves resources, but raises the risk of pauses if synthesis falls behind reading.

How many syntheses the Kokoro engine can process at the same time (the only voice engine with this option today — the others already process one synthesis at a time). Standard (2) is faster and was tested on a real device. Reduced (1) processes one at a time — slower, but uses less processor at once. Nothing above 2 is offered because it was never tested.

How many syntheses the Supertonic (onnx) engine can process at the same time. Standard (1) always processes one at a time — how Supertonic has always worked in the app. Concurrent (2) is EXPERIMENTAL: it may make reading more fluid, but the native engine\'s safety for simultaneous calls was never tested on a real device — there is a real risk of the synthesis process crashing mid-book (contained: the main app won\'t crash, but reading may fail and need a retry). resources.string: Converts books into high-quality audiobooks using Microsoft Edge TTS and Google Gemini TTS, directly on your device.
EPUB · PDF · TXT · MD · DOC · DOCX · MOBI

Defines the speech synthesis service used for conversion.

• Edge TTS (Microsoft): free, requires internet. Offers many voices in several languages.

• Gemini TTS (Google): more natural and expressive voice. Requires a Google API key.

• ElevenLabs: official ElevenLabs voices, using your own API key.

• OpenRouter: multi-model TTS (OpenAI, ElevenLabs). Requires an OpenRouter API key.

Controls the silence inserted between paragraphs during narration.

• 0ms: no pause, continuous reading.
• 300-600ms: natural pause, recommended for most texts.
• 900-1500ms: longer pauses, useful for technical texts or studying.

Longer pauses slightly increase audio generation time.

Defines the bitrate of the generated MP3 file.

• 64 kbps: smaller file, lower quality.
• 128 kbps: standard quality, good balance.
• 192 kbps: high quality.
• 256 kbps: maximum quality, larger files.

Note: bitrate is applied by Gemini TTS + FFmpeg. Edge TTS uses its own codec.

The app stores synthesized audio chunks in cache.

This avoids reprocessing identical sections when converting the same file again or resuming an interrupted conversion.

Clear the cache to free storage or force a full re-synthesis.

To clone a voice, the app needs a free file from Kyutai, the company that created Pocket TTS. You will do 4 simple steps, only once:

1. Sign in to the Hugging Face website with a free account
2. Accept Kyutai's terms of use
3. Download the file (about 220 MB, Wi-Fi is best)
4. Bring the file into the app

You sign in only in your browser. The app never sees or stores your password.

You need a free account on the Hugging Face website. If you already have one, tap I have an account. If not, tap Create free account: the website opens in your browser. After creating it and confirming your email, come back here.

Tap Open page. In your browser, sign in, read the terms and tap the button that agrees and gives you access. The terms forbid cloning another person\'s voice without their clear permission. Then come back here.

Choose the language of the voice you will clone and tap Download. Your browser will save a file called model.safetensors (about 220 MB). Wait for the download to finish and come back here. If the website asks you to accept the terms, go back to step 2.
